transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mikael Johansson (Redwood CSM), Jared Lim (Nimbus Head of AI), Asha Patel (Nimbus Platform Eng), Carlos Mendez (Nimbus Security), Lina Zhou (Nimbus Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Reviewed week-over-week latency and token-cost deltas across three candidate models; flagged two catalog items with 'entanglement' (incompatible KV/cache profiles) for deeper vetting.
- Agreed on an emergency hatch (hot-fallback) procedure: route 20% to a cheaper quantized variant + 10% to hosted fallback during high error rates, with canary gating and rollback timeouts.
- Action items: share benchmarking CSV, run outage tabletop, provide prompt distribution.

Topics:
- Model selection delta (v1.4 vs v1.5-q4)
- KV/prefix cache compatibility and catalog entanglement
- Hot-fallback/emergency hatch plan (routing percentages, canary rules)
- Security/compliance asks for Private deploy consideration
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we'll go ahead and get started. um Jared, you said 15:00 UTC works?
[00:06] Jared: Yeah that's great, thanks Ethan.
[00:08] Asha: Morning from my side, afternoon for you all - quick heads up, I might drop to mute for a bit when I triage infra logs later.
[00:15] Priya: Cool. I'll run us through the benchmarks first, then we can talk fallbacks and security.

[00:28] Priya: So slide-ish, uh summary from the run we did on Friday — we compared three catalog variants: redwood-v1.4 (float32), redwood-v1.5-quant (8-bit), and third-party-compat-2. From a median latency perspective under our simulated ramp: v1.4 is 180 ms median, v1.5-q around 220 ms but cost per token ~0.6x, and third-party-compat had the worst tail at 1.1s at 95th.
[01:05] Lina: Can I interrupt - when you say "cost per token 0.6x" is that after accounting for batching improvements?
[01:11] Priya: Good call — yes that includes the batching profile we used for your 50RPS baseline and prefix KV cache hit assumptions at 30%. If cache hit drops to 10% the gap widens.
[01:22] Jared: We saw a few production flaps last week that looked like cache invalidation storms - could that explain the widened tail?
[01:28] Priya: Exactly, the reason we used "entanglement" in the notes is that some models rely on a different KV layout and the cache warmup is incompatible across variants. So if you route traffic between v1.4 and v1.5-q without a warming strategy, you'll get a spike in long tail latency.
[01:46] Asha: So that explains our spike. When we spun the 10-node staging set the cache was cold every deploy, which matched the outage pattern.
[01:54] Ethan: Ok so mitigation options we discussed: canary warmups, prefix pinning to avoid mixing keys across variants, or route-by-session so session hits stick to a model family. Which is most realistic for you?
[02:08] Jared: Route-by-session seems easiest given our frontend session token, but we wanted to avoid maintaining per-session model-state for all users. Over time we want sticky routing for 24h then allow rebalancing.
[02:20] Priya: That is doable. Our runtime supports sticky routing with optional TTL. There's a small overhead to maintain mapping but it's minimal — like an extra lookup at request time.
[02:30] Carlos: Quick sec — from security perspective, if we do cross-routing do we create any new data residency concerns? We need to ensure encrypted context doesn't leak between compute zones.
[02:39] Priya: Good question. We can constrain routing by region and by VPC. So the traffic never leaves the allowed compute pool. It only becomes an issue if you bring models into Private where customer controls the KMS - then we need to validate keys and tokenization.
[02:55] Carlos: Got it, please capture KMS diagram as an action item.

[03:10] Mikael: Also quick note — last week we had an internal bug where the fallback policy was mislabelled so the system routed to third-party-compat-2 instead of the intended quant variant; we've patched the policy engine.
[03:23] Asha: That explains the odd cost spike on Friday.

[03:30] Priya: Back to the catalog comparison — the "entanglement" list has two bad apples: third-party-compat-2 (incompatible KV schema) and a smaller custom quant build that doesn't honor prefix caching. We recommend either re-quantizing to match prefix format or exclude them from soft-fallbacks.
[03:52] Jared: Excluding is fine short term. Long term we want to standardize quant profiles so ops isn't chasing format mismatches.
[03:59] Priya: Yep — that's where Redwood Optimize recommendations come in, we can push a suggested quant profile for your workload.

[04:10] Ethan: Let's talk emergency hatch: the ask was a way to degrade gracefully when error rates or 95th latency cross a threshold without disrupting user flows, right?
[04:18] Jared: exactly. Ideally auto-routing to a cheaper and more stable variant and a staged degrade rather than a full stop.
[04:25] Priya: Proposal from our side: gate by error-rate and 95th-latency window. If 95th>750ms for 2 minutes we trigger hatch1: shift 15-20% traffic to redwood-v1.5-quant with session pin TTL 1h. If errors continue and 95th>1s for 3 minutes trigger hatch2: spill additional 10% to hosted fallback (latency fast but slightly different behavioral profile), maintain canary monitoring for 10 minutes then escalate to wide spill.
[04:54] Lina: How do we monitor behavioral regression? We can't just drop quality.
[04:58] Priya: We'll shadow a sample and run automatic quality checks on a small prompt set you provide — similarity and hallucination heuristics. If quality drops beyond threshold we won't advance to the next hatch stage.
[05:12] Jared: Are those heuristics customizable? We may have domain-specific checks for clinical safety.
[05:16] Priya: Yes you can supply your prompt set and we can add custom comparators — and Redwood has a safe-guard that can route to human review instead of automated fallback if safety thresholds trip.

[05:30] Ethan: Carlos, from compliance side, is the idea of routing to hosted fallback acceptable? Or does that violate policy?
[05:37] Carlos: Hosted compare is ok for non-PHI subsets, but any PHI processing must stay in private VPC with customer-managed keys. So the hatch policy must be policy-aware — disallow hosted for PHI classes.
[05:48] Ethan: That is doable — we can add request-level metadata flags and routing rules.

[06:02] Jared: Ok so practically what do we need this week? Lina - prompt distribution, Carlos - KMS diagram & list of compliance gates, Ethan/Priya - updated spreadsheet with simulated cost/latency under hatch scenarios.
[06:12] Lina: I can get the prompt hist by EOD Wednesday.
[06:15] Carlos: KMS diagram and contacts by next Monday, good.
[06:19] Priya: We'll re-run the targeted bench after we receive prompt hist to line up sequence length percentiles — that will refine the 95th estimates.

[06:35] Speaker 1: [inaudible] — there's a question in chat about competitor behavior and feature parity.
[06:41] Ethan: Right, quick note on that — Anthropic product can do similar sticky routing but they charge premium for private, and OpenAI hosted fallback is faster but less configurable in routing policies. Worth considering for specific latency needs but tends to be more expensive.

[07:00] Asha: For the tabletop outage simulation, how long should our on-call be prepared? We can block a two-hour window Thurs.
[07:07] Mikael: Two hours is perfect; we'll do a 45-60 minute walkthrough and then 30-45 minutes of war-room style role play. Priya will inject faults.
[07:18] Priya: I'll prepare two scenarios: cold cache + traffic spike, and control-plane misrouting where policy engine flips route.

[07:28] Jared: I'd like to add a third: KMS rotation during hatch. We had a kube-ops event that rotated keys and we lost access to a model for a few minutes.
[07:36] Carlos: Yup rotate is a big one for security. We'll include that.

[07:45] Lina: small nit — is there a way to reduce the KV warming time? Right now it takes ~20 seconds to warm on a session basis.
[07:50] Priya: Two options: prepopulate hot prefixes during deploy or keep a tiny warm pool that primes the cache. Both add cost; warm pool is more reliable for low-latency needs.
[08:03] Jared: We'll run cost analysis on warm pool.

[08:10] Ethan: Ok let's go into a quick demo of the policy engine — Priya, you take it away.
[08:15] Priya: Sure, sharing screen... [small pause, background typing] This is the route policy UI — you can set TTLs, percentages, canary windows, and also attach predicates like request.meta.pii=false. Here I toggle hatch1 to 20% and set the quality shadow to 5% shadow traffic.
[08:40] Asha: Looks straightforward; can we version-control these policy definitions?
[08:44] Priya: Yes, policies are stored as JSON with version IDs and simple rollout semantics; we also keep audit logs.
[08:51] Carlos: Audit logs are good — can you confirm retention levels for logs? We need at least 1 year for audits.
[08:57] Priya: Audit logs retention is configurable; our default is 90 days but enterprise plan supports 2 years. We'll include that in the security doc.

[09:10] Ethan: Quick check — anyone on the call opposed to the proposed hatch percentages?
[09:15] Jared: No objections, sounds reasonable as long as quality monitors gate the progression.
[09:20] Asha: Agreed.

[09:30] Priya: Alright final housekeeping: I'm going to add the two catalog items to the "no-soft-fallback" list in your staging config and we'll re-quantize the smaller build as an SRE plan.
[09:43] Lina: When you say re-quantize does that require us to provide full checkpoints or just the tokenizer/weights?
[09:48] Priya: Depend on the build, sometimes we can take your checkpoint, run an offline quant and produce a compat layer, other times we'll ask you to produce a new quant artifact. We'll document specifics per model.

[10:00] Mikael: Ok everyone good to wrap? Quick recap of owners in chat as well.
[10:06] Ethan: Thanks all — we'll send the spreadsheet and benchmark notes. Look out for the invite for Thursday's tabletop.
[10:12] Jared: Thanks team.
[10:15] Carlos: Thanks.
[10:18] Asha: Bye.
[55:30] [call ends]

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 1) and small word swaps introduced by the transcriber; timestamps are approximate.
